title: Vendor publish: technical acceptance + copy scaffold
body:
Purpose:
This is a working scaffold for vendor/publisher listings that combines the technical acceptance checklist with ready-to-drop-in copy variants and UX microcopy. Goal: reduce back-and-forth with partners by (1) making acceptance criteria explicit, (2) providing copy options for different UX placements, and (3) surfacing legal/metadata needs up front.

Status and usage notes:
- Draft: iterate with Solutions and Legal before finalizing.
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (GTM). Secondary: Owen Brooks (PM), Leila Zhang (Design).
- Use this doc as the single source to send to publishers during preflight. Attach manifest + screenshots + test credentials.

1) Acceptance checklist (technical & ops) – tick boxes we send to partner
- [ ] Basic manifest present (product name, short id, SKU mapping table)
- [ ] Package metadata: version, region availability, supported runtimes, endpoints
- [ ] Security posture: SOC2 / ISO statements (or equivalent) attached
- [ ] Network configuration: VPC peering / IP allowlist instructions included (if required)
- [ ] Auth + keys: sample curl + SDK snippet, instructions for scoped API keys
- [ ] Billing & metering: sku IDs for trial, paid tier, overage; sample invoice itemization
- [ ] Audit logs: where to find usage logs and retention policy (clarify if > 90 days)
- [ ] E2E smoke tests: sample requests, expected response shapes, max token lengths
- [ ] Monitoring hooks: recommended metrics and labels (latency_ms, tokens_generated, error_rate)
- [ ] Feature gating: required flags or entitlements to toggle during canary
- [ ] Rollout plan: canary %, start date, rollback criteria
- [ ] Accessibility check: alt text for images, keyboard access for trial UI flows
- [ ] Legal artifacts: CLA/MOU, data processing agreement (DPA) or link to signed DPA

Notes on tests: include 3 smoke tests that intentionally hit the streaming path, the cached-path, and a long-sequence path (>= 2k context) so we validate kernel/kv fallback behavior. Provide sample tokens so we can reproduce token-count billing.

2) UX placements & copy targets
- Marketplace tile (short): 1–2 lines, 60 characters preferred.
- Marketplace detail page (long): 3–5 short paragraphs, up to ~1200 chars.
- Feature bullets: 3–5 bullets, each 6–12 words.
- Trial CTA microcopy: 2 variants (free trial / request demo)
- Onboarding modal header: 6–8 words; follow-up paragraph: 1–2 sentences with a link to docs

3) Ready copy variants (drop-in) – pick A or B and minor-customize
- Tile (A): "Serve high-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and cost."
- Tile (B): "Fast, resilient LLM inference for production apps — optimize cost & latency."

- Detail page short lead (A): "Redwood-backed deployment for low-latency model serving. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployment modes and get predictable token economics and built-in fallbacks for high availability."
- Detail page short lead (B): "Ship LLM features with confidence. Our inference runtime routes, caches, and quantizes to meet SLAs while keeping per-token costs transparent."

- Feature bullets (pick 3):
  - "Multi-mode deployment: hosted API, dedicated capacity, private VPC."
  - "Smart routing and automatic fallbacks across regions and model variants."
  - "Token-level observability and per-route cost breakdowns for optimization."
  - "Built-in batching, KV prefix caching and quantization suggestions to lower cost."
  - "SLA-backed latency targets for enterprise deployments."

- Trial CTA variants:
  - CTA A (Free trial): "Start 14-day free trial — no credit card required"
  - CTA B (Request demo): "Book a quick demo — see throughput & latency in action"

- Onboarding modal example:
  - Header: "Connect & test: quick start in 5 minutes"
  - Body: "Create an API key, run the sample request, and view token & latency metrics in Console. See quickstart guide -> [link to docs]."

4) Microcopy for technical snippets (for code blocks)
- Curl sample intro: "Run this curl to validate your token and endpoint."
- Error guidance short: "If you see 403, check API key scope and IP allowlist."
- Quota guidance: "Burst quota is best-effort; for sustained throughput, request Dedicated."

5) Metadata & assets required from partner
- Primary logo: SVG and 2 raster sizes (120x120, 600x200) with alt text
- 3 screenshots: console UI, latency dashboard, billing sample (annotated)
- Short legal blurb: one-sentence product description for marketplace legal page
- Support contact: email and response SLA (e.g., 24–48 hours)

6) Legal / compliance checklist (red flags to escalate)
- [ ] Requires data residency beyond offered regions (escalate to Legal + Infra)
- [ ] Partner wants open-ended access to raw customer prompts (must sign DPA + SAM clause)
- [ ] Mismatched terms: partner TOS requires <12 month audit windows (we normally require 90+ days retention)
- [ ] Partner requests changes to our listing copy that affect security claims (e.g., "bank-grade encryption") — require evidence

7) QA matrix (sample tests we run internally before publish)
- Test 1: Listing metadata validation (fields present, SKU mapping correct). Outcome: pass/fail
- Test 2: Billing smoke (simulate small usage and verify invoice line items). Outcome: pass/fail
- Test 3: Integration smoke (partner endpoint responds and return shapes match contract). Outcome: pass/fail
- Test 4: UX preview (tile + details render on marketplace preview, mobile & desktop). Outcome: pass/fail
- Test 5: Accessibility audit (basic axe scan + manual tab order). Outcome: pass/fail

8) Rollout playbook (summary)
- Step 0: Send this scaffold + manifest to partner; collect artifacts. Owner: GTM
- Step 1: Tech review & security sign-off (SRE + Security). Owner: Eng-SRE
- Step 2: Legal & billing sign-off. Owner: Legal / Finance
- Step 3: Publish to sandbox preview. Owner: Marketplace PM
- Step 4: Partner validation window (3 business days)
- Step 5: Schedule pub date and post-publish QA (24–48h). Owner: GTM + QA

9) Communication templates (short)
- Email to partner (send with scaffold):
  Subject: "Marketplace Listing Preflight: actions required"
  Body: "Hi — attaching our acceptance scaffold. Please share requested artifacts (manifest, logos, screenshots, signed DPA if applicable) within 7 business days so we can schedule your preview publish. Reach out to maya@redwood.ai for questions."

- Slack internal escalation snippet:
  "FYI: Partner X ready for marketplace preview. Need security review + billing SKU mapping. Linking GTM-4123."

10) Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm who is authoring the short legal blurb (GTM or Partner?).
- Confirm standard trial period for marketplace (14 vs 30 days) — decision pending finance (JIRA: GTM-4178).
- Should we include a pre-baked demo key for partners to use in preview? Security has concerns.
- Decide canonical image alt text format: [ProductName] logo — used on listing.

Notes-to-self / quick wins:
- Create a one-page PDF checklist from this scaffold to attach to partner outreach emails.
- Add a small JSON manifest schema example at the bottom (later) to speed up partner integrations.
- Capture common copy edits to build a small copy-snippet library for reuse.

Appendix: Example manifest snapshot (informal)
- product_id: redwood-rr-inference
- title: "Redwood Inference — hosted API"
- short_description: "Hosted API for predictable LLM inference."
- skus: [trial_small, standard_monthly, enterprise_reserved]
- regions: [us-west1, eu-west1]

End.
